title: Menes
summary: Menes is named in Cory, Ancient Fragments (1876, ed. Hodges), with a reign length or synchronism. Display only.
description: Added from the Cory import. Display only. Cory gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not a BC year this record can sort on, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Cory is display-only and gives none).

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 112; Manetho, ap. Syncellus, Chronicon 54 to 59, and Eusebius, Chronicle 14 and 15
reign.note: Menes the Thinite, first of eight kings. He perished by a wound from a hippopotamus. Eratosthenes (p. 138) prints the same 62 years for Mines (Menes).

reign.date: “He reigned sixty-two years, and lived in the year of the world 2,900”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 138; Eratosthenes, ap. Syncellus, Chronicon 91, 96, 101, 104, 109, 123, 147
reign.note: The edition's parenthesis is Mines, (Menes). The dynasty list (p. 112) prints 62 years. From the second king, each printed year of the world equals the previous king's year plus the previous king's reign (our check, not a figure of the text). Anno Mundi is not stored and is not converted.

reign.date: “Menas (i.e., Menes), was the first king of the Egyptians”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 200; Diodorus Siculus, Hist., Book ii
reign.note: No new length. The next sentence, two descendants for more than 1,400 years, is not his reign.
